text:
sophia: Quick note from today's bring-up: magnet-14b-int8v2, long priming (~3200 tokens) + 600-token continuation. We see a deterministic content "skip" / topic hop around continuation token ~+90.

omar: Short config paste? especially rope params + any tiling/window flags.

sophia: Args: `--quant=int8v2 --rope-mode=scaled --rope-base=12000 --kv-window=4096 --kv-tiling=enabled --kv-prefetch=async`
Priming verified at 3218 tokens. Continuation consistent across runs.

lee: Does fp16 baseline reproduce? if not, points to quant / int8 rounding affecting rot positional math or indexing.

sophia: fp16 keeps correct continuation. Suspect either: prefetched KV misindexed (tile boundary) OR rotary-phase aliasing exacerbated by quant.

ana: (ana): Can you dump per-layer KV checksums + rot-phase summary at the flip point? Also try toggling `--kv-tiling=disabled` and `--kv-prefetch=off`.

sophia: Doing that now. Added `--kv-index-verify=on` to the run.

qa-bot: Test harness id: 20260321-smoke-42, pool: canary-gpu-9. Artifacts: gs://redwood-evals/m14b/int8v2/4300002222/

omar: If it's tiling, I'd expect the checksum flips to align to tile boundaries across layers (e.g., every 512 tokens). If it's rope aliasing, the offset moves when you change rope-base. Did you vary rope-base?

sophia: Yes: rope-base=12k => flip ~+90. rope-base=48k => flip ~+310. rope-base=unscaled => no flip (but int8 run without scaled rope not supported normally).

lee: That pattern smells like phase aliasing: scaled rope compresses phase resolution and quant noise pushes layer phases over a rounding boundary. But why would KV index / tiling matter? maybe prefetch merges partial KV chunks with different quant rounding, causing per-token phase jumps.

ana: Grepped the checksums: at continuation token 89 -> layer 10 key checksum changes sign, layers 9/11 unchanged. At token 90 -> layer 22 flips. Not a clean tile boundary pattern.

omar: Hmm layered stagger suggests accumulation of small per-layer quant deltas hitting a threshold at different times. Let's compute per-layer cosine similarity between pre/post-quant K vectors for priming tokens 0..3200 and monitor drift accumulation.

sophia: I added cos-sim logging. Preliminary: mean cos-sim per layer drops from 0.997 -> 0.92 across priming, with a few layers dipping below 0.88. Those layers correspond to checksum flips.

lee: Try a targeted repro: copy the priming tokens but truncate to first 1600 and re-run continuation — does flip still occur at same continuation offset (relative to priming length) or absolute token index?

sophia: Good check. Truncated priming (1600) reproduces flip but at continuation offset ~+ (90 + (3200-1600) modulo window) -> suggests absolute window/tiling interplay.

ana: Action items I propose: 1) Run with `--kv-prefetch=off` and `--kv-tiling=disabled`. 2) Run int8v2 with added per-layer scale bias compensation (temporary patch to reduce quant rounding on Q/K). 3) Add a checksum delta aggregator to flag early drift (before user-visible token shift).

omar: Also capture tokenization boundary around the flip: sometimes token splits cause local semantics shift and quant noise amplifies it. Attach the token ids around the flip.

qa-bot: Run queued: 4300002233 (no-prefetch), 4300002244 (no-tiling), 4300002248 (int8v2-compensate). ETA ~8m.

sophia: Thx. If no-prefetch/no-tiling eliminates the issue we should default to disabled in int8 canaries until a fix. Will update with artifacts + minimal repro script.

lee: If deterministic and tied to quant, escalate to eng-runtime. This can break long-context customers. mark P0 if reproduced on stable infra.

sophia: On it. I'll post the artifact summary (checksums, cos-sim plots, token ids) when runs finish.
